note: The walker's figure (doc 23, W5; approved October 21, 2026): Matt's Meshy model, split into a body and two arms in nTop and coloured per vertex by tools/figure-prep/prep.py (assets/figures/walker.glb). The rest pose is the A-pose: the arms hang down by the rig. Metres, y up, body +z forward, feet on y = 0. bones: name, parent, pivot (the arms' pivots come from the model's extras, so a new prep moves them). skin: where each part blends between bones, as anchors along a height (y) or along the arm (t, m out from the shoulder). hang: the arms' resting direction. gait: per pace, step length, foot lift, arm swing, lean and the rise and fall of the hips; wade blends in by the water's depth. springs: the hat tip, coat skirt and pack follow a beat late (stiffness per second squared, damping 0..1 of critical). eyes: the two ovals the shader draws on the head (rest pose), their colour, a faint glow after dark (cd per m2), blinks and expressions. poses: sit, kneel, feed, the arrivals, and the keeper's camp acts (crawl, drink, pitch, lay, strike, crawlIn, climbOut; see actsNote). All motion is drawing only: it reads the walker and never changes it.

body.note: What the creature pass reads: the soft contact shadow (scaleReal sizes it, times displayScale), displayScale: the figure is drawn this much of the model (October 21, 2026: 0.737, so you stand 1.4 m tall, not 1.9 m, and creatures read larger beside you; the eyes, contact shadow and all the motion (gait, poses, ground under the feet) follow it, src/world/figure/motion.js works in body meters), the cloth's sheen (none) and the eye bones for a wet glint (none: the eyes are drawn).

gait.note: Paces by speed in body meters a second (the walker's speed divided by body.displayScale, so a smaller figure takes a longer pace for its size and quicker steps); stepM, liftM and the rest are body meters too. The figure blends between them by the speed it is given. stance: share of a stride a foot is down.

arms.note: The walking arm swing's shape (the swing itself is each pace's armDeg). elbowForward: radians of extra elbow bend per radian of forward swing; elbowBack: how much the elbow straightens on the back swing, the same way; across: how far a forward swing comes in across the body, per radian of swing.

springs.note: The parts that follow a beat late. hatTip.accelGain: how far the tip tips back as you speed up (and forward as you stop). skirt.strideSway: how far the coat skirt swings to the side of the forward knee, per meter the knees are apart front to back; skirt.speedFlare: how far it flares back per body meter a second. pack.tiltGain: radians the pack tips per meter it lags the body's rise and fall; pack.rock: share of the hips' twist the pack rocks with.

footprints.note: Prints (W6): each step that lands on sand, or on bare earth and mud, leaves a soft print the shape of the boot's sole, darkening the ground by darkness; it fades over fadeH game hours, and is gone once the tide covers it. Not on grass or rock (minWeight: how much of the ground must be sand or soil), not under water deeper than dryM. Never saved: the island forgets you between visits. soleM is in world meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model). max: how many at once (the oldest go first).

grass.note: Grass underfoot (W6): blades lean away from the walker and press a little flatter: under the body within bodyM (sitM when sitting), and where each of the last steps landed within footM, springing back over springS seconds. World meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model).

poses.actsNote: The keeper's camp acts (docs/future/13-keepers-camp.md 2.3; October 22, 2026), played by walk.act(name) and src/world/figure/acts.js. posture: the walker's posture while it plays (for presence and the view); after: its posture once done. keys: at t seconds in, kneel and crawl (0..1, how far into each posture), lean and head (extra degrees forward and down; negative leans back or looks up), drop (the hips lower, body m), arms (0..1, how much the hands follow l and r) and l, r (where the left and right hand reach, body m: x left, y over the ground under you, z ahead). A key changes only what it names; the rest carries on from the key before, easing between. The last key's t is the act's length, and walk:act-done comes then. crawl: the hands-and-knees pose crawlIn ends in, held until climbOut or a walk (hipDeg tips the hips, pelvisZ brings them forward over the knees). ease.actInS: an act blends in from the posture it began in; ease.stepLiftM: a foot that moves far as the posture changes lifts this high on the way, a step and not a slide.
